GeoPulse – NEXTRONZ

Smart Disaster Monitoring and Early-Warning System

GeoPulse is an innovative disaster monitoring and early-warning prototype developed by Team NEXTRONZ, inspired by the geographical challenges of Wayanad, Kerala. We developed an integrated system using ESP32 technology, multiple environmental sensors, an ESP32-S3 camera, IoT connectivity and GSM communication.

The system monitors temperature, humidity, rainfall, soil moisture, gas levels, vibration, movement and ground orientation using sensors connected to an ESP32 DevKit V1. An ESP32-S3-CAM provides live video streaming, allowing users to observe the monitored surroundings remotely. Sensor readings are displayed on a 2.8-inch TFT screen and a mobile-friendly Wi-Fi dashboard featuring real-time values, graphical analysis, historical data and warning messages.

A SIM800L GSM module provides emergency SMS notifications and automatic phone calls to configured contacts. Audible warnings are also provided for selected rain and soil-moisture conditions.

GeoPulse addresses the challenge by combining environmental monitoring, visual observation and multiple alert methods in one affordable prototype. It is important because timely awareness of changing environmental conditions can support better preparedness and faster responses. Our vision is to make disaster monitoring more accessible, understandable and useful for communities in vulnerable regions.

GeoPulse – NEXTRONZ

Smart Disaster Monitoring and Early-Warning System

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

GeoPulse is an intelligent disaster monitoring and early-warning prototype inspired by the geographical and environmental challenges of Wayanad, Kerala. It is designed to monitor environmental changes and identify conditions that may indicate potential landslide and earthquake-related risks.

The system uses an ESP32 DevKit V1 connected to multiple sensors, including an MPU6050 accelerometer and gyroscope, vibration sensor, soil moisture sensor, rain sensor, MQ-2 gas sensor, DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, and PIR motion sensor. These sensors continuously collect environmental and movement-related data. The ESP32 processes the readings and identifies abnormal conditions using programmed threshold values.

An ESP32-S3-CAM provides live video streaming through Wi-Fi, allowing users to observe the surrounding environment using a mobile phone. A 2.8-inch ILI9341 TFT display shows sensor readings and system status.

A dedicated Wi-Fi dashboard provides real-time sensor values, graphical representations, historical readings and warning messages. The SIM800L GSM module enables emergency SMS notifications and automatic phone calls to two configured mobile numbers. It can also support incoming calls and SMS with suitable programming. A buzzer provides audible warnings for selected rain and soil-moisture conditions.

2. What benefits does it provide?

GeoPulse combines several monitoring technologies into one system. It helps users observe environmental changes, monitor rainfall and soil conditions, detect unusual vibrations and movement, and view the surroundings through a live camera stream.

The dashboard makes sensor information easier to understand through graphs and warning messages. GSM communication provides another way to receive alerts when internet connectivity is unavailable, provided cellular coverage is available.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact of GeoPulse is to improve environmental awareness and support disaster preparedness, particularly in geographically vulnerable regions.

By combining sensor monitoring, live visual observation and multiple communication methods, the project aims to help communities and monitoring teams identify potentially concerning environmental changes earlier and respond more effectively.

It also demonstrates how affordable electronics and connected technologies can contribute to community-focused disaster preparedness.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware and software were used?

Hardware components:

- ESP32 DevKit V1 microcontroller
- ESP32-S3-CAM camera module
- MPU6050 accelerometer and gyroscope
- Vibration sensor
- Soil moisture sensor
- Rain sensor
- MQ-2 gas sensor
- DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor
- PIR motion sensor
- SIM800L GSM module
- 2.8-inch ILI9341 SPI TFT display
- Buzzer
- Power supply and connecting wires

Programming languages:

- C/C++ for ESP32 firmware
- HTML for the web dashboard
- CSS for dashboard design
- JavaScript for live dashboard updates and graphical visualization
- JavaScript with Node.js for the dashboard server

Software and development tools:

- Arduino IDE / ArduinoDroid
- ESP32 board support package
- Arduino libraries for sensor communication and display control
- Node.js
- Android mobile browser
- Blynk platform for IoT integration

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of GeoPulse lies in integrating multiple monitoring features into a single affordable prototype. Instead of depending on only one sensor or one communication method, it combines environmental sensing, ground movement monitoring, live camera streaming, a visual TFT interface, a web-based dashboard and GSM-based communication.

The combination of graphical sensor histories, live camera observation and SMS and phone-call alerts provides different ways to understand and communicate environmental conditions.

The project also focuses on making technical information accessible through a mobile-friendly dashboard, allowing users to monitor multiple sensor readings from one place.

6. What factors did our team consider?

Our team considered the following factors during development:

1. Affordability: Selecting accessible and relatively low-cost electronic components.
2. Environmental relevance: Monitoring rainfall, soil moisture, vibration and other environmental conditions relevant to disaster preparedness.
3. Real-time monitoring: Displaying updated sensor information and camera footage.
4. Communication reliability: Combining Wi-Fi and GSM communication to provide alternative alert channels.
5. User accessibility: Designing a dashboard with understandable readings, graphs and warning messages.
6. Power requirements: Considering suitable power supplies for the ESP32, camera and GSM module.
7. Modularity: Designing the system so that sensors and features can be tested and improved separately.
8. Safety and reliability: Considering sensor calibration, false alerts, connectivity failures and the limitations of a prototype.
9. Future development: Allowing additional sensors, improved data analysis and more advanced warning features to be integrated.
GeoPulse – NEXTRONZ demonstrates how embedded systems, environmental sensors, IoT technology, live camera streaming and cellular communication can be combined to support disaster preparedness. Our vision is to develop an affordable, accessible and expandable monitoring system that helps people understand environmental changes and become better prepared for potential natural hazards.
